head: On every high street.
Gone in six weeks.
slides.sub: How a 99-year-old British chain ran out of room to fail.

image.label: A shuttered high-street store with a closing-down sign
image.brief: 2008년 겨울 영국 소도시 하이스트리트. 셔터가 반쯤 내려진 대형 잡화점 앞 '폐점 세일' 안내문, 젖은 보도와 크리스마스 조명. 실제 로고나 간판 디자인 없음.

head: Sweets, records, toys.
Everything, cheap.
body: Woolworths opened its first British store in Liverpool in 1909. For generations it sold a bit of everything at low prices.
Children spent pocket money at the pick 'n' mix counter. Families bought their singles, school supplies and Christmas presents there.

image.label: Children choosing sweets from bins in a busy shop
image.brief: 1970~80년대 영국 잡화점의 셀프 사탕 코너 앞에서 사탕을 고르는 아이들. 따뜻한 향수 어린 톤. 아이들 얼굴은 일반적인 모습으로, 로고 없음.

head: Then everyone else
sold the same things.
body: By the 2000s, big supermarkets sold DVDs, toys and sweets next to the groceries, often for less. Online shops and downloads took the music and films.
Woolworths was still selling a bit of everything. Others now did each part better.

image.label: A supermarket aisle full of DVDs and toys
image.brief: 2000년대 영국 대형 슈퍼마켓 통로. 식료품 옆에 DVD와 장난감이 쌓여 있음. 밝은 형광등, 브랜드 로고 없음.

head: Your stores are worth a lot.
What do you do?
body: It's around 2001. Your parent company is spinning you off and wants cash. You own many of your shop buildings.

options.text: Keep the buildings, even if it means less cash now
options.feedback: Your money stays tied up in property, but no landlord can raise your costs. Keep swiping.

options.text: Sell the buildings and rent them back
options.feedback: You get a large sum today, and a rent bill every year after. Keep swiping.

options.text: Sell only the weakest stores and keep the best
options.feedback: Less cash up front, but you keep your strongest sites. Keep swiping.

image.label: Keys on a property contract on a desk
image.brief: 사무실 책상 위 부동산 계약서와 열쇠 꾸러미. 2000년대 초 영국 사무실 분위기, 차가운 회색 조명.

head: Cash for the parent.
Rent for the stores.
body: Before Woolworths was split off from Kingfisher in 2001, many of its store buildings were sold and leased back.
The cash went out the door. What stayed was a long list of rents that had to be paid whether sales rose or fell.

image.label: A rent invoice taped to a shop counter
image.brief: 상점 계산대 위에 붙은 임대료 청구서. 비어 가는 진열대가 뒤로 흐릿하게 보임.

slides.label: Woolworths stores across the UK when it collapsed
body: Sales were weak and costs were fixed. When the 2008 credit crunch hit, suppliers reportedly lost insurance cover and wanted tougher terms. In late November 2008, Woolworths went into administration.

image.label: A map of Britain dotted with store pins
image.brief: 수백 개의 핀이 꽂힌 영국 지도. 핀 몇 개가 하나씩 빠져 떨어지는 장면.

slides.label: jobs lost as the chain closed, according to reports
body: A buyer reportedly offered £1 for the stores, but no deal was done. Closing-down sales ran through Christmas, and the last stores shut in early January 2009.

image.label: Empty shelves and a final sale sign
image.brief: 텅 빈 진열대와 '마지막 세일' 안내문. 직원 실루엣이 불을 끄는 장면. 얼굴은 보이지 않게.

head: The name survived.
The shops didn't.
body: Shop Direct bought the brand and relaunched it as a website. It closed in 2015.
People still loved the memory of Woolworths. They had simply stopped needing it for anything in particular.

image.label: A laptop screen glowing in a dark room
image.brief: 어두운 방에서 빛나는 노트북 화면, 일반적인 쇼핑 사이트 화면. 실제 브랜드 디자인 없음.

head: No clear reason to visit,
no cushion for a shock.
body: Woolworths was stuck in the middle: not the cheapest, not the widest range, not the most convenient.
Selling its buildings turned flexible costs into fixed rents. When sales fell, those rents ate what little margin was left.

image.label: A store squeezed between two giant buildings
image.brief: 거대한 두 건물 사이에 끼어 있는 작은 상점 일러스트. 차분한 그래픽 톤.

head: Fondness isn't a reason.
Give one to buy.
body: Customers can love a brand and still shop elsewhere. Fixed costs make that drift fatal when bad times come.
**Try it today:** name one thing customers can get only from you, and check what you'd still owe if sales fell by a third.

image.label: A single bag of sweets on an empty counter
image.brief: 텅 빈 계산대 위에 놓인 사탕 봉지 하나. 해 질 녘 빛, 로고 없음.

신용보험사가 납품업체에 대한 보증을 줄여 납품 조건이 나빠졌다는 내용과, 소매 부문을 1파운드에 인수하겠다는 제안이 있었으나 성사되지 않았다는 내용은 2008년 11월 보도 기준입니다. 카드에는 'reportedly'로 표시했습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1파운드 인수 제안과 은행의 거절 확인.
Shop Direct가 브랜드를 인수해 온라인으로 재출시했다가 2015년에 문을 닫았다는 내용은 당시 보도로 확인하세요.
